[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: + is addition, which is commutative and associative, so 2 + 3 + "bc" and "bc" + 2 + 3 must give the same thing. Java rule: when one operand of + is a String the other is converted to a String and concatenated, and + is evaluated left to right, so 2 + 3 + "bc" is "5bc" but "bc" + 2 + 3 is "bc23".
[1] misconception (M) -> StringPlusLeftToRight: wrong rule: 2 + 3 + "bc" and "bc" + 2 + 3 give the same text. Right rule: + is evaluated left to right: 2 + 3 + "bc" is "5bc" but "bc" + 2 + 3 is "bc23".
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> StringPlusLeftToRight: Points to LT (+ is applied left to right, each + deciding between addition and concatenation from its two operands at that moment). Applied unevenly: once a String has appeared the student goes back to numeric addition for later terms, or concatenates two numbers that come before any String. (here mixing in: "2 + 3 + "bc" and "bc" + 2 + 3 give the same text")

[0] names_the_element (N): String conversion is the automatic conversion of a non-String operand of + into its String form when the other operand is a String (also done for print/println arguments).
[1] states_the_rule (S): When either operand of + is a String, the other operand is converted to a String and the result is the characters of the first followed by those of the second; System.out.print and println also convert any argument to a String.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Evaluate + operators left to right (same precedence, left-associative): at each +, if either current operand is a String, convert the other and concatenate; otherwise add numerically. Parenthesized parts are evaluated first.
[1] output_prediction (OP): A String: 2 + "bc" is "2bc", 2 + 3 + "bc" is "5bc", "bc" + (2+3) is "bc5", "bc" + 2 + 3 is "bc23", "1234" + 99 is "123499".
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Concatenation creates a new String and changes no variable; state changes only by assignment, e.g. String c = a + b; with a = "1234" and int b = 99 gives c the value "123499".

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Conversion happens first, then concatenation: the non-String operand is turned into its characters before the two Strings are joined.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Used to build output messages and labels from computed values, e.g. System.out.println(a + " + " + b + " = " + c);.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> StringPlusLeftToRight: Adding parentheses around the numeric part changes "bc23" into "bc5"; moving a String operand earlier turns every later + into concatenation; the order of operands matters, unlike numeric addition.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use string conversion with + to produce output and labels; do not use it to do arithmetic on numeric text (parse first), and parenthesize numeric parts that must be added before concatenation.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: + is left-associative, so terms after a String are concatenated, not added. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: A numeric sum written after a String without parentheses, e.g. "Sum: " + a + b printing "Sum: 34" for a = 3, b = 4.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Only + converts to String; other arithmetic operators are not defined on Strings. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: Using -, *, / with a String operand, e.g. "Hello" - 1 or "12" * 2.
